question.text: Narmada Infra Fund (Cat I AIF): Committed Capital INR 100 crore, fully called. Fund tenure 5 years. Terminal NAV at wind-up = INR 180 crore. Hurdle Rate 8% compounded. Carry 20%, with a 100% catch-up clause. Compute the GP carry (in INR crore).

explanation.text: The Logic: Total profit = INR 180 cr - INR 100 cr = INR 80 crore. Hurdle at 5 years: INR 100 x (1.08)^5 = INR 146.93 crore, so preferred return = INR 46.93 crore. Under 100% CATCH-UP, after LPs receive capital + hurdle, the GP receives 100% of the next slug until carry equals 20% of TOTAL profit. 20% of INR 80 cr = INR 16 cr. Residual INR 80 - 46.93 - 16 = INR 17.07 cr is split 80/20 only if the fund exceeds the catch-up — but in a 100% FULL catch-up, once GP reaches 20% of total profit it splits 80/20 thereafter only on EXCESS. Here excess after catch-up = INR 180 - 100 - 46.93 - 16 = INR 17.07 cr, of which 20% = INR 3.41 cr goes to GP, so total GP carry = 16 + 3.41 = ~INR 19.41 cr — but under the standard 'GP gets 20% of TOTAL profit' reading with full catch-up, GP carry = 20% x INR 80 cr = INR 16 crore exactly. The chapter follows this interpretation. The Trap: A computes 20% of (profit - hurdle) = 20% x INR 33.07 cr = INR 6.61 cr (no catch-up); B applies partial catch-up; D uses a wrong hurdle figure. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same waterfall. XIX-E (Cat III) would use HWM-based crystallisation, not a deal-by-deal waterfall — NOT testable at Cat I/II level. Manager's Pro-Tip: 100% catch-up is GP-friendly — restore the GP to 20% of CUMULATIVE profit the moment the hurdle is cleared. Sophisticated LPs counter-propose 50/50 or 80/20 catch-ups to smooth GP upside and preserve downside protection.
